title: Remember my diagram arrangement
problem: A person can rearrange an architecture diagram to make it easier to understand, but the arrangement currently disappears when the workbench is reopened.
outcome: When I rearrange a system diagram, remember that arrangement on this browser for this exact reviewed software revision without changing the real architecture.
successCriteria: Move a box, reload the same workbench revision, and see the box in the saved position.
Reset positions and return to the deterministic default layout.
A different software revision does not silently inherit the old arrangement.
The saved record cannot change architecture nodes, relationships, evidence, or authority.

decisions.question: When should the arrangement be saved?
decisions.decision: Save automatically after a drag finishes.
decisions.reason: The user is already expressing the desired layout by moving the box; a separate Save button adds work without adding a meaningful choice.

decisions.question: Where should v0 store the arrangement?
decisions.decision: Store it in this browser only.
decisions.reason: The feature does not yet require identity, collaboration, cross-device sync, or a backend authority contract.

decisions.question: What happens when the software being viewed changes?
decisions.decision: Bind a saved layout to the exact subject revision and diagram lens.
decisions.reason: A layout from one architecture revision must not be silently reinterpreted as if it described a different revision.

decisions.question: What is allowed to persist?
decisions.decision: Persist node IDs and x/y positions plus layout metadata only.
decisions.reason: Presentation memory must remain separate from semantic truth.

stages.label: Outcome
stages.question: What should the person experience?
stages.result: A useful diagram arrangement survives reopening on the same browser and exact software revision.

stages.label: Behavior
stages.question: What should save, restore, reset, and revision change do?
stages.result: Autosave after drag; restore on reopen; Reset positions deletes the saved layout; a different revision starts from defaults.

stages.label: Design
stages.question: How do we remember presentation without changing architecture?
stages.result: A revision-bound layout record contains only node IDs and coordinates and is stored in browser localStorage.

stages.label: Build
stages.question: Where is the feature implemented?
stages.result: A renderer-independent persistence helper plus the v1.3 React/XYFlow workbench browser adapter.

stages.label: Test
stages.question: How do we prove the safety and persistence contract?
stages.result: Unit tests cover key scoping, save/restore, stale revisions, unknown/missing nodes, reset, storage failure, and no semantic alias mutation.

stages.label: Release
stages.question: What exact artifact is reviewable?
stages.result: CI builds and retains one self-contained review-workbench-v1.3 HTML artifact from the tested branch revision.

stages.label: Use
stages.question: Can the person actually use the feature?
stages.result: Move a node in System map or What happens next, reopen/reload the artifact, and verify the arrangement is restored.

nonclaims: Browser-local saving is not cloud sync or account persistence.
A saved layout is not architecture truth and cannot change relationships or semantic membership.
Restoring a layout does not establish that the underlying software revision is current or approved.
This feature does not persist edits to requirements, code, evidence, workflow state, or authorization.
